messages.author: 6db62e08ec862130
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: where does all the command/arg stuff go now?
parts:
On Tue, Mar 10, 2015 at 09:48:17AM +1100, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> I should also add what my first mentor at SpeechWorks told me
> when I asked how version control could possibly work:
>
> Merge before everyone else and then it's there problem!
>
> There is some wisdom in this: smaller, shorter-lived branches
> are the way to go.

I think the way you permit/encourage free-wheeling merging is part of
the problem. Linear history created with more rebasing and limited
merging is much easier to understand than the dense web of merges that
appears in the stan repo.

A good reason to make a merge commit is if somebody else contributed the
changes and your role is only to merge them. You might merge your own
branch too if there is a sequence of commits that are related to the
same logical change.

In my opinion.

--
Joshua N. Pritikin
Department of Psychology
University of Virginia
485 McCormick Rd, Gilmer Hall Room 102
Charlottesville, VA 22904
http://people.virginia.edu/~jnp3bc
